core.title: Telemetry tests assert on emission
core.given: A test identified as a telemetry test — by its URN carrying one of the profile's telemetry kind segments, or by matching the profile's telemetry-test filename pattern (colocation alone identifies the test, even without a URN kind segment)
core.when: the test exists in the suite (every telemetry-identified test, new, changed or unchanged, is scanned)
core.then: The test MUST contain an emission assertion: an assertion that the emitter was called or that the event was emitted, in one of the profile's emission-assertion idioms.
prefer: Inject a spy or captured emitter and assert the emission: pass a test double for the emitter into the unit under test, exercise the unit, and assert that the expected event was emitted with its payload.
avoid: Asserting only the return value in a telemetry test: it proves the function ran, not that the event fired.
unless: Only telemetry-identified tests are in scope; tests identified by neither the telemetry URN kind segments nor the telemetry-test filename pattern are not scanned.
core.why: The event is the entire point of a telemetry test: dashboards, alerts and downstream analytics are built on the emission, not on the return value.
evidence: Every telemetry-identified test (telemetry URN kind segment or telemetry filename pattern) contains at least one emission assertion; the stack's telemetry-discipline check reports no findings.
verification: Telemetry-test identification: a telemetry URN kind segment OR the profile's telemetry-test filename pattern; either signal is sufficient on its own — filename colocation is accepted alongside the URN without a kind segment.
The check tests only for the presence of one of the profile's emission-assertion idioms in an identified telemetry test; it does not evaluate the substance of the assertion.

Scope: only telemetry-identified tests are scanned — all of them, regardless of whether they changed; only those with no emission assertion are flagged. Non-test source files that emit telemetry are not covered.
Severity 3; disposition strict: the check fails on every finding, with no advisory mode and no ratchet baseline.

fires: A test whose designation marks it as a telemetry test (telemetry kind segment on its URN, or telemetry filename colocation) only asserts on the unit's return value.
A telemetry-identified test file contains a test with no assertion that the emitter was called or that the event was emitted, even though its designation comes from the filename alone.
An existing, unchanged telemetry-identified test without an emission assertion is found when the suite is scanned.
doesNotFire: A test with no telemetry designation in a file not matching the telemetry-test filename pattern (not telemetry-identified, not scanned).
A telemetry test that asserts the emitter was called with the expected event and payload.
Non-test source files that emit telemetry.

proposedKeys.meaning: Name pattern that marks a test file as a telemetry test by filename colocation (identification by colocation alone).
proposedKeys.whyNoExistingKey: suffix.<file_kind> is parametric only over the general file kinds (source, unit_test, acceptance_test, e2e_test, markup, plan_artifact, config); none covers a specialized telemetry-test file kind.

proposedKeys.meaning: URN kind segments by which a test identifies itself as a telemetry test.
proposedKeys.whyNoExistingKey: urn.<artifact> and urn.binding.<artifact> describe URN shapes and bindings for the listed artifact kinds (component, acceptance, ...); no key describes kind segments carried on a test's URN.

proposedKeys.meaning: The stack's assertion idioms that count as an emission assertion (spy/mock call matchers on the emitter, or expectations on emit-style methods).
proposedKeys.bunValue: toHaveBeenCalled / toHaveBeenCalledWith / toHaveBeenCalledTimes on the emitter, or an expectation on .emit / .emitted / .capture / .track / .record
proposedKeys.whyNoExistingKey: The idiom group has no key for test-assertion constructs; existing idiom keys describe source, markup and boundary idioms only.

neutralityNotes: The obligation itself is fully neutral (a telemetry-designated test must assert the emission, not only the return value). Three concrete inputs had no existing vocabulary key and are proposed: the telemetry-test filename pattern (suffix.telemetry_test), the telemetry URN kind segments (urn.telemetry_kinds) and the emission-assertion idioms (idiom.emission_assertion); without these keys the core cannot state how a telemetry test is identified or which assertions satisfy it. activation.facts[1] was re-expressed from the non-neutral fact name path_glob to file_kind 'telemetry_test', whose concrete pattern comes from the profile. Concrete matcher/spy API examples, the .ts extension example, the Convex-sibling provenance remark and the detector/validator id remain bunOnly; per-rule severity 3 and strict disposition are kept in core:verification rather than the profile.
